classification.difficultyReason: Derives all capacity-compatible occupancy patterns and changes the symmetry correction for each when labelled cabins become indistinguishable.

content.prompt: A hostel has three labelled cabins $A$, $B$ and $C$. Each cabin contains three indistinguishable beds. Six backpackers arrive. How many ways can they be assigned to cabins (no capacity exceeded) if

answer.short:
$510$ ways.

Add the occupancy cases $(3,3,0)$, $(3,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$, retaining the cabin capacity restriction.
answer.worked:
The possible occupancy patterns are $(3,3,0)$, $(3,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$.

For $(3,3,0)$, choose the empty cabin, then choose three backpackers for one of the occupied cabins. For $(3,2,1)$, assign the three different occupancies to the labelled cabins in $3!$ ways, then choose the groups. For $(2,2,2)$, choose two backpackers for $A$, then two for $B$; the remaining two go to $C$.

$$\begin{align*}N&=3\binom{6}{3}+6\binom{6}{3}\binom{3}{2}+\binom{6}{2}\binom{4}{2}\\N&=60+360+90\\N&=510.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$450$ ways.

Subtract the $(3,3,0)$ allocations from part (a).
answer.worked:
An empty cabin forces the occupancy pattern $(3,3,0)$. Subtract these allocations from part (a).

$$\begin{align*}N&=510-3\binom{6}{3}\\N&=510-60\\N&=450.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: cabins are indistinguishable? (The backpackers only wanted to know who is going with who, without caring which cabin they end up in.)

answer.short:
$85$ ways.

Count the same three occupancy patterns, dividing by $2!$ for the two equal groups of three and by $3!$ for the three equal groups of two.
answer.worked:
Use the occupancy patterns $(3,3,0)$, $(3,2,1)$ and $(2,2,2)$.

For $(3,3,0)$, divide by $2!$ because the two groups of three are indistinguishable. For $(3,2,1)$, group sizes distinguish the groups, so no division is required. For $(2,2,2)$, divide by $3!$ because the three groups of two are indistinguishable.

$$\begin{align*}N&=\frac{\binom{6}{3}}{2!}+\binom{6}{3}\binom{3}{2}+\frac{\binom{6}{2}\binom{4}{2}}{3!}\\N&=10+60+15\\N&=85.\end{align*}$$
